{"world_model":"W5 (contrarian), after E057. The tip is still E049 at 5.198 s. Across three builds, seeds 0–2 read 0.7535, 0.7552 and 0.7536, and time ran 5.198–5.223 s.

1. Rebuild noise mostly reshuffles seeds rather than shifting the mean. The 3-seed spread across E049 builds is ≤0.17 pp, consistent with a per-seed SD of ~0.25 pp. I expect E057's 20-seed means to differ by ≤0.06 pp, which would refute H4.5.1. Rebuild time spread is ~0.5%.

2. Elementwise and optimizer traffic is the hidden cost, and I keep under-pricing it (misses on E046 and E056).
   - A frozen group saves its fused BN/GELU backward, which is H6.5/H6.6.
   - It also saves its separate Muon call: an fp32 momentum buffer plus bf16 Newton-Schulz on each filter, run through its own reduce-overhead graph.
   - The mechanism nobody has proposed: the Muon step is three separately compiled update graphs that run every step, even in the 20 px phases where conv compute is small. NS cost does not depend on resolution, so in the low-resolution phases it is a much larger share of each step than the 32 px profile suggests. Levers:
     - batch the NS across groups into one graph;
     - run NS at lower precision or with fewer iterations (steps=3 already);
     - update group-3 filters every other step at 20 px.
   - Any lever that trims per-step fixed cost would show up as E046/E056-style surprise time wins.

3. Muon renormalizes the filters and fixes the update norm. So a filter's ||ΔW||/||W|| just follows its LR schedule, and I094's filter curves are uninformative. The BN-bias and gradient-norm curves might separate some cases, but freeze cost looks roughly linear in the LR integral removed while downstream layers still learn, not like a threshold:
   - E037: −0.4 pp
   - E055: −0.15 pp
   - E053: ~−0.2 pp

4. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not. E026 and E033 were free. Step cuts traded at or slightly below the dial's rate (~1–1.5 s/pp).

5. The whitening bias runs at 64× LR. If it is detached at 6%, it stays fitted to 20 px antialiased patch statistics, while the input distribution keeps shifting through 24/28/32 px. That likely costs a little. The 20% detach covers only the 20/24 px phases, and that one was free.

6. Settled by reading the code:
   - BN scale is already frozen, so I092 needs no run.
   - Only fine labels are supplied, so H1.8 is blocked.
   - Filter wd is inert because the filters are renormalized.

7. The end-game is at a local optimum: averaging, LS schedule and LR floor all hurt (E025, E030, E032, E044).

8. Best paths:
   - (a) Re-keep E052 (4.99 s) under a derived gate. Its population mean is probably ~0.752, which clears the official 0.75 with high probability. The binding constraint is the single-build seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 check (~50%).
   - (b) The ReLU swap plus a small epoch top-up, stacked on E052.
   - (c) Fusing the Muon/NS updates into a single graph.

9. On the PCIe judge, expect times 5–10% higher.

W5 (contrarian), after E057. The tip is still E049 at 5.198 s. Across three builds, seeds 0–2 read 0.7535, 0.7552 and 0.7536, and time ran 5.198–5.223 s.

1. Rebuild noise mostly reshuffles seeds rather than shifting the mean. The 3-seed spread across E049 builds is ≤0.17 pp, consistent with a per-seed SD of ~0.25 pp. I expect E057's 20-seed means to differ by ≤0.06 pp, which would refute H4.5.1. Rebuild time spread is ~0.5%.

2. Elementwise and optimizer traffic is the hidden cost, and I keep under-pricing it (misses on E046 and E056).
   - A frozen group saves its fused BN/GELU backward, which is H6.5/H6.6.
   - It also saves its separate Muon call: an fp32 momentum buffer plus bf16 Newton-Schulz on each filter, run through its own reduce-overhead graph.
   - The mechanism nobody has proposed: the Muon step is three separately compiled update graphs that run every step, even in the 20 px phases where conv compute is small. NS cost does not depend on resolution, so in the low-resolution phases it is a much larger share of each step than the 32 px profile suggests. Levers:
     - batch the NS across groups into one graph;
     - run NS at lower precision or with fewer iterations (steps=3 already);
     - update group-3 filters every other step at 20 px.
   - Any lever that trims per-step fixed cost would show up as E046/E056-style surprise time wins.

3. Muon renormalizes the filters and fixes the update norm. So a filter's ||ΔW||/||W|| just follows its LR schedule, and I094's filter curves are uninformative. The BN-bias and gradient-norm curves might separate some cases, but freeze cost looks roughly linear in the LR integral removed while downstream layers still learn, not like a threshold:
   - E037: −0.4 pp
   - E055: −0.15 pp
   - E053: ~−0.2 pp

4. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not. E026 and E033 were free. Step cuts traded at or slightly below the dial's rate (~1–1.5 s/pp).

5. The whitening bias runs at 64× LR. If it is detached at 6%, it stays fitted to 20 px antialiased patch statistics, while the input distribution keeps shifting through 24/28/32 px. That likely costs a little. The 20% detach covers only the 20/24 px phases, and that one was free.

6. Settled by reading the code:
   - BN scale is already frozen, so I092 needs no run.
   - Only fine labels are supplied, so H1.8 is blocked.
   - Filter wd is inert because the filters are renormalized.

7. The end-game is at a local optimum: averaging, LS schedule and LR floor all hurt (E025, E030, E032, E044).

8. Best paths:
   - (a) Re-keep E052 (4.99 s) under a derived gate. Its population mean is probably ~0.752, which clears the official 0.75 with high probability. The binding constraint is the single-build seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 check (~50%).
   - (b) The ReLU swap plus a small epoch top-up, stacked on E052.
   - (c) Fusing the Muon/NS updates into a single graph.

9. On the PCIe judge, expect times 5–10% higher.

Unsure:
- whether a correlated build component exists;
- ReLU's population cost;
- how much of the per-step fixed cost the Muon update really takes at 20 px.

forecasts.reason: E052/E053 population ~0.752 with small build SD; the fresh-seed deficit vs E049 should be ≤0.15 pp and P(official≥0.75) high. Seeds 0–2 on one build are a coin flip.
Δtime ~0.12 s fits, but a ~0.1 pp Δacc on 20 seeds plus build SD is ~1σ, so the dial will not be resolved.
TrainingData carries only fine labels and a hard-coded table counts as external data, so it is blocked; if anything is measured, it is the tip.
The BatchNorm class already sets weight.requires_grad=False, so it closes by reading the code; no change.
Saves ~14% of steps × a small whitening-backward share at 20/24 px (~0.3–0.5%), below rebuild noise. A bias frozen at 20 px stats may cost ~0.05–0.1 pp.
Muon renormalizes the filters with a fixed-norm update, so filter ΔW/W tracks the LR schedule. Freeze costs scale with the LR integral, not a threshold, so the curves won't separate E028 from E037.

cruxes: What share of a 20 px or 24 px step is the three separately compiled Muon/NS update graphs plus fused SGD and Lookahead? If it is ≥25%, a fused single-graph optimizer is the next E046/E056-style surprise time win.
Do E057's three 20-seed means of E049 differ by more than 0.06 pp (a correlated build component)? This sets whether E052 at 4.99 s can be re-kept under the derived gate.
What is the ReLU swap's 20-seed population cost on fresh seeds? If it is ≤0.15 pp, ReLU plus a +0.25 epoch top-up stacked on E052 is ~4.85 s.
